c.tagline: A tri-border jungle town beside one of the world's most spectacular waterfall systems
langs: Portuguese and Guarani (common given the tri-border location)

card: Widely accepted; cash (preferably USD for exchange) useful for smaller shops

taxi.fareNote: Most visitors take a tour bus or taxi directly to the national park entrance

emergency.note: 911 is the general emergency line in most of Argentina; 107 specifically reaches medical services

walk: Downtown Puerto Iguazú is walkable; Iguazú National Park is about 20 min away and requires a bus, taxi, or tour

safety.safety: Very safe town, popular with international visitors
safety.crime: Petty theft near the falls' crowded walkways is the main concern

hood_landmark.Downtown Puerto Iguazú: Puerto Iguazú's central Avenida Victoria Aguirre
hood_landmark.Selva Iryapu / Guarani Community: The Yryapú Guarani indigenous community reserve

avoid.reason: There are no true no-go zones, but skip unlit back streets near the port and riverfront border area late at night.
Petty theft around the bus terminal and aggressive coatis and monkeys snatching food at the falls are the main nuisances.

hood_desc: The town center with most hotels, restaurants, and tour operators; a practical, unglamorous base a short drive from the falls.
A Guarani indigenous community and forest reserve near the national park, offering cultural and ecological tours.

The park itself, about 14 km east of town: rainforest crossed by the Upper and Lower Circuits, the Ecological Train out to the Devil's Throat catwalk, and boats into the spray at the base of the falls. Exactly one hotel stands inside the gates, so staying here means walking the circuits before the day buses arrive and after they leave.

water.note: Locals drink the tap water, but most visitors stick to bottled in this humid border town.

transit.sys: Local urban buses connecting downtown to the national park entrance
transit.map: Not centrally published; buses run frequently to the park from the downtown terminal
transit.note: A direct bus service connects downtown Puerto Iguazú to the national park entrance

transport.air: Cataratas del Iguazú International Airport (IGR), about 20 min from downtown and close to the national park
transport.bus: Long-distance buses connect to Buenos Aires (about 18-20 hr) and Posadas
transport.car: Rental cars available; the Tancredo Neves Bridge connects to Foz do Iguaçu, Brazil

net.m: Good 4G coverage in town, patchier within the national park
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A Movistar, Claro, or Personal tourist SIM or eSIM

landmarks: Garganta del Diablo (Devil's Throat)
The thunderous centrepiece of Iguazú Falls, an 80-metre horseshoe cataract reached by catwalks where mist and rainbows engulf awestruck visitors.
Iguazú National Park Upper and Lower Circuits
UNESCO-listed jungle walkways threading past dozens of cascades, coatis and toucans, delivering ever-changing panoramas of the world's greatest waterfall system.
Hito Tres Fronteras
An obelisk viewpoint above the meeting of the Iguazú and Paraná rivers, where Argentina, Brazil and Paraguay converge in a single sweeping vista.
Isla San Martín
A rocky island in the heart of the falls, reached by boat, whose short trails put you at eye level with roaring cataracts.
Sendero Macuco
A tranquil seven-kilometre rainforest trail inside the national park, rewarding hikers with monkeys, butterflies and the secluded Arrechea waterfall and swimming hole.
Güirá Oga Wildlife Refuge
A jungle sanctuary rehabilitating rescued toucans, monkeys and harpy eagles, offering guided walks through the Atlantic Forest on the road to the falls.
La Aripuca
A monumental structure of salvaged giant tree trunks shaped like an indigenous trap, celebrating Guaraní culture and rainforest conservation with regional crafts and yerba-mate ice cream.
Jardín de los Picaflores
An enchanting private garden in town where dozens of iridescent hummingbirds of many species swarm feeders just centimetres from your camera.
Casa Ecológica de Botellas
An ingenious family home and workshop built entirely from recycled bottles and cartons, offering inspiring tours on sustainable living in the jungle.
Parque das Aves (Bird Park, Foz do Iguaçu)
Just across the Brazilian border, this rainforest aviary lets you walk among flamboyant toucans, scarlet macaws and butterflies in immense walk-through enclosures.

train.note: No railway serves Puerto Iguazú. Argentina's only international passenger train is the Posadas-Encarnación shuttle to Paraguay, about 300 km south. Arrive by coach or fly into Puerto Iguazú airport.

intl.to: Foz do Iguaçu (Brazil) - across the Tancredo Neves bridge
intl.op: Río Uruguay / Crucero del Norte — tickets on board or at the terminal

intl.to: Ciudad del Este (Paraguay) - via Foz do Iguaçu

bus.note: This is a tri-border town and the cross-border buses are ordinary local services running every 20-30 minutes from the Puerto Iguazú terminal, costing very little. They do not always wait while you clear immigration, so if you need an entry or exit stamp tell the driver and be prepared to catch the next one. Long-distance coaches to Buenos Aires take about 18 hours; book through Plataforma 10 (https://www.plataforma10.com.ar/).

ferry.note: There is no scheduled passenger ferry - all three border crossings here are by road bridge. The boats that run beneath the falls on both the Argentine and Brazilian sides are adventure excursions rather than transport.

half.name: Cataratas do Iguaçu (Brazilian side)
half.blurb: Brazilian park entrance across the border offers a panoramic walkway facing the falls from the opposite bank of the river.

half.name: Itaipu Dam
half.blurb: Hydroelectric dam near Foz do Iguaçu, about 45 minutes away, is among the largest power plants in the world and offers guided tours of its structure.

half.name: Ciudad del Este
half.blurb: Duty-free border city across the Friendship Bridge, about 40 minutes away, is packed with electronics markets and shopping malls.

full.name: San Ignacio Miní
full.blurb: Red sandstone ruins of a 17th-century Jesuit mission, about three hours south, are among the best preserved of the Jesuit reductions in South America.
